title: Reduce routing entropy and modernize fallback stack
creator: Maya Chen
description: Refactor the smart routing layer to reduce state entropy, simplify the policy evaluation path, and replace ad-hoc fallback chains with a single composable failover primitive. Goals: reduce tail latency from routing, make fallbacks auditable, and eliminate race conditions observed during regional failovers.
background: Over the past year we've accumulated several quick fixes in the routing hot path: per-region heuristics, multiple independent rollback paths, and bespoke shims to support older policy formats. Incidents #INC-2025-11 and #INC-2025-27 highlighted a race between the affinity updater and the fallback registrar that causes duplicate fallbacks and metric skew. Current code is hard to reason about and blocks future work (policy-level A/B rollouts).
success_metrics: 10% reduction in p99 routing latency for 99th-percentile requests
All routing decisions include a stable trace-id for debugability
acceptance_criteria: New fallback primitive deployed behind flag and exercised in staging
No increase in median latency (±5%) with feature flag on
All regional affinity updates are deterministic and covered by unit tests
End-to-end canary that exercises cross-region failovers passes for 3 consecutive hours
tasks: Design: formalize fallback interface and edge cases (Maya)
Implementation: introduce FailoverCoordinator and replace ad-hoc registrars (Liam)
Migration: adapter that maps legacy policy payloads to new evaluator (2 engineers)
Testing: add deterministic unit tests for concurrent affinity updates and an integration harness that replays incident traces
Observability: attach trace_id to routing decisions and add dashboard for fallback counts
notes: We decided to prioritize a single-threaded coordinator owning fallback transitions to reduce lock complexity. Trade-off: slightly larger memory footprint due to explicit transition queues, but we gain linearizable semantics and easier observability. We will keep the legacy registrar as an adapter behind a feature flag for two weeks of canary, then flip and remove the adapter in a follow-up cleanup task.
implementation_summary: Phase 1: Add FailoverCoordinator service with an evented transition queue and idempotent transition ops. Phase 2: Migrate policy evaluators to emit candidate lists to coordinator rather than performing direct region swaps. Phase 3: Kill legacy registrars and run tidy-up PRs.
pr_links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/4231 - add test replay harness for INC-2025-11
testing_plan: Run unit tests (concurrency and idempotence) in CI. Deploy feature flag to staging, exercise canary with 5k synthetic requests per minute using real traffic profiles. Run incident trace replay tool against staging to validate determinism. Promote to canary prod with 10% traffic after 72h of no regressions.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy to staging. 2) 24h smoke + replay validation. 3) Canary in prod at 10% for 72h. 4) Gradual ramp to 100% over 48h if green. 5) Remove legacy adapter 14 days after full rollout.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: coordinator becomes bottleneck - Mitigation: implement sharded coordinator keyed by region-affinity
Risk: adapter mismatch drops edge-case policies - Mitigation: log and fallback to legacy registrar for unknown payloads during canary
Risk: increased memory on hosts - Mitigation: stress-test hosts in staging and increase heap limits if necessary
